jobs.title: Technical Partner Enablement Manager
jobs.description: Sarvam Circle, our partner ecosystem, is one of our fastest growing vectors. It brings in firms to take frontier AI to government and public institutions, enterprises, and MSMEs across the country. Certified partner engineers building on our stack extend that reach at a breadth and pace that compounds. Every firm that gets good at building on Sarvam widens what all of our work reaches. There is a version of partner-built AI that actually works. Where a partner's engineers hold the same bar our own engineers do, where the playbooks are good enough to travel, and where a customer gets the same system whoever is in the room. That bar exists because Sarvam's engineers set it. Carrying it outward intact is what this role does, and it is the part most companies never solve. This is a hands-on technical role, not a pre-sales one. You own the engineering core of Sarvam Circle: how partner engineers get certified on our stack, what standard their work is held to, whether they can run an engagement without a Sarvam engineer beside them, and whether what they ship holds up. Done well, a large share of everything Sarvam delivers runs through the capability you built. Headquartered in Bengaluru and founded by leading AI researchers, Sarvam builds foundational models for Indian languages, enterprise AI platforms, and voice-first AI agents that serve hundreds of millions of Indians. Sarvam is backed by top-tier investors and works with national and state governments, large enterprises, and developers across the country. We are building the AI layer for a billion people. WHAT THIS ROLE PROMISES YOU You shape the engine, not just run it Sarvam Circle already has the firms and the momentum. Training and enablement is central to how Sarvam works with its partners, and how that actually operates is being designed now: the certification, the quality bar, the onboarding, the scorecards, the standard a partner engineer is held to. You are early enough to own its shape, at a company growing this fast. Leverage over headcount Your output is not what you deliver, it is what several hundred engineers across multiple firms are capable of delivering. The ceiling on your impact is set by how well you build the system. You work at the source Sarvam builds the whole stack: the foundational models, the infrastructure they run on, and the products on top. When a partner hits something the platform does not do yet, you are in a room with the people who built it. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the technical relationship with a set of partner firms: what their engineers can build, how much certified capacity they hold, and the quality of what they ship. - Build the certification programme. Define what a partner engineer must demonstrate before they touch a Sarvam deployment, and run the process that gets them there. - Own partner enablement: the playbooks, tooling, training and access partner teams need to build on the Sarvam stack without a Sarvam engineer beside them. Our engineers author the technical build playbooks; you own whether they exist, are current, and are legible enough for someone outside Sarvam to execute. - Translate Sarvam's platform, models and product surface into something a partner's engineering team can build with. Most of the leverage in this role is in how well you do this. - Shape how a partner gets used on an engagement: which firm fits the work, where in the engagement they come in, and how the build splits between their engineers and ours. - Lead the first co-delivered engagement with a new partner, hands-on, and own the readiness call on whether they can run the next one independently. - Own the review cadence with partners. It is what keeps us close to the work: where each engagement stands against plan, where the risk sits, and what has to change before a date slips. - Hold the quality bar across the partner base: scorecards, an honest read on whether partner-built work matches our own standard, and corrective plans when it does not. We bring together CPaaS, CCaaS, and Voice AI to help businesses manage customer conversations across voice and digital channels. Our platform powers billions of customer interactions globally , enabling enterprises to connect with their customers at scale, automate conversations, and deliver seamless experiences. With a strong presence across India, APAC, the Middle East, and Africa , Exotel works with thousands of businesses across industries. We are building the next generation of AI-powered customer communication, where intelligent voice and digital experiences become an integral part of how businesses engage with their customers. At Exotel, you’ll work in a fast-paced, high-ownership environment alongside teams across Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success, solving complex problems at scale and shaping the future of customer communication. Job Location: Gurugram/ Bengaluru About the Role You own retention and expansion of Exotel's domestic enterprise business — a large, revenue-critical share of our named accounts, already paying us in at least one SKU across CPaaS, CCaaS, and Voice AI / voice-bot streaming. The first job is to defend that base. These accounts are already running revenue-critical infrastructure on Exotel, and protecting and expanding that, before anything else, is what this role is accountable for. The second job is the whitespace inside this base. The average paying account today uses only a fraction of our full portfolio, which spans CPaaS, CCaaS, and Voice AI. Most of these customers are proof the product works — they just haven't been sold the rest of what we do. This role owns both: hold the base we've already won, and grow their footprint from there. This is not a support role and not a coordination role. You are the single named owner of Net Revenue Retention for enterprise India, and the frontline escalation point when anything in the customer's experience (delivery, support, billing, product, or platform) breaks. When a strategic account has a problem that spans multiple internal teams, you run it end-to-end until it's resolved, not until it's routed. What You Own 1. Retention & Expansion — the revenue mandate Own NRR and GRR for the full domestic enterprise book, reported and defended monthly against target. Build the account-level whitespace model that turns average SKU attach — currently ~1.5 products per paying account — into a prioritised, quota-bearing cross-sell funnel across CPaaS (voice, SMS/WhatsApp/RCS), CCaaS (ECC/Harmony), and Voice AI/voice-bot products, focused on the accounts we've already converted. Own account tiering and segmentation (strategic / growth / maintain) so QBR depth, executive coverage, and expansion effort are allocated by risk and headroom, not by who escalates loudest. Partner with Sales leadership on renewal forecasting and the handoff line between net-new logo acquisition and install-base expansion, so no account falls into the gap between the two. 2. Customer Governance & Executive Engagement Own the QBR program end-to-end: cadence, content standard, and executive attendance, Build and maintain an account health-score model (usage depth, support load, sentiment, commercial trajectory) that flags churn or expansion risk before it shows up in a renewal conversation. Act as the named executive sponsor for the top tier of strategic accounts. 3. Escalation Ownership & Cross-Functional Orchestration Be the single accountable owner of enterprise customer escalations — running point across Delivery, Support, Finance, Tech, and Product until resolution, with authority to pull the right people into a room. Define and enforce a severity framework and SLA for escalations, so "pillar to post" becomes a repeatable operating process with clear ownership at each stage, not a hero act each time. Build the structured feedback loop from escalations and expansion conversations into the product roadmap — this team sees where the product is costing revenue before anyone else in the company does. 4. Team Leadership Hire, structure, and lead the enterprise Customer Experience team (Account/Relationship Managers and CSMs) — define role charters, account/territory assignment, and career paths. Run the team's operating cadence: weekly pipeline and risk reviews, monthly business reviews, and a quarterly NRR readout to company leadership.
